noticeable.why: 'the context is not making an adjustment, I mean, of course, our whole position ... is that it means making an adjustment' contradicts itself, so a careful reader would likely notice. Y says yes. X says no; the 'I mean' could be read as a self-correction, so X is partly right.

stakes.why: Both say yes: the lawyer's position is reversed.

rule.why: Both say the rule is right.

blind.why: X picks the reference in both orders, pointing to the contradiction with the next clause. Y's pick flips: it picks the reference in order 1, then in order 2 argues 'is not' sets up a needed contrast and picks the engine's version.

misses.why: Both list the added 'not' at severity 4 and nothing else. X's 'what' note just repeats the reference words, a small blemish.

overall.why: On the negation control, X picks the reference in both blind orders as it should; Y's pick flips with the order. Y is a little better on noticeable.
